property_summary: After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any sender, target, and emergency, the configured state variable remains true.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable must remain true.

After any public call that triggers the _governanceApproved flow, the configured state variable should remain true because only successful proposals can change it and endConfiguration is the only way to set it to true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any sender, target, and emergency, the configured state variable remains true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable remains true if it was already true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the contract's configured state variable must be true if the sender is a successful proposal.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved(address,address,bool) with arbitrary arguments, the DAO address remains unchanged from its initial value set in the constructor.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved(address,address,bool), the DAO address is unchanged from the constructor value.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, DAO equals the address of the test contract (the initial constructor argument).
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address equals the test contract (initial constructor argument).

After calling assertGovernanceApproved, c.DAO() is either the test contract (initial value) or the address that was passed as the first argument to assertGovernanceApproved, but never the original caller if it differs from both.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, DAO must be equal to the initial DAO address that was set in the constructor.
The DAO address after any call to assertGovernanceApproved must equal the address passed to the constructor.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the stored DAO address must equal the address that was provided to the constructor.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, DAO must be nonzero (not address(0)).

The mutation flips the requirement for setting DAO: originally allowed only if sender equals DAO (or DAO unset or not configured); now allows only if sender is NOT DAO, so setting DAO from DAO itself reverts.
The rule: after calling assertGovernanceApproved with emergency=false, the caller (which is also the DAO) can still call setDAO to change the DAO address.
setDAO can be called only when caller is DAO or DAO address is zero or configured is false
After assertGovernanceApproved reverts, the DAO address remains unchanged and can still be set by a non-DAO caller.
Calling setDAO with any address does not revert when configured is false and the caller is the current DAO (or DAO is zero).
After a successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address is unchanged when called back through the same function.
After assertGovernanceApproved reverts, the DAO address can still be set by a caller that is not the original DAO.
When the sender is not the DAO and not governed, assertGovernanceApproved always reverts before any state change.
The setDAO function can only be called when DAO is address(0), or the caller is the current DAO, or the contract is not configured; otherwise it must revert.
After assertGovernanceApproved completes successfully (not reverting), the state variable DAO remains unchanged from its initial value.
After assertGovernanceApproved completes successfully, the value of DAO is unchanged from the initial deployment value.
After assertGovernanceApproved completes successfully, the value of DAO returned by public getter remains equal to the DAO address passed in the constructor.
After any successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the public getter c.DAO() returns the address that was set during deployment, not address(0).
After any successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the public getter c.DAO() must be equal to the DAO address passed in the constructor.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved on the reference contract, the DAO state variable remains unchanged (equal to its initial constructor value), while on the buggy contract it may change.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the state variable DAO remains equal to its value before the call.

For any given address k, after a successful call to assertGovernanceApproved(k, target, emergency) (i.e., the call does not revert), the governed[k] mapping becomes true in P but false in M when the isGoverned parameter for k is false.
After assertGovernanceApproved, the setGoverned mapping reflects the state set by the most recent setGoverned call with equal-length arrays.
After calling setGoverned with two arrays that have the same length, the mapping update for each index is determined by the same index position in both arrays.
After setGoverned is called with equal-length arrays, iterating over the mapping from 0 to governables.length-1 shows that governed[governables[i]] is set to isGoverned[i].

After calling setGoverned with equal-length arrays, the mapping governed[governables[i]] is set to isGoverned[i] for all indices i, and any subsequent call to assertGovernanceApproved does not alter this mapping for those indices.

After setGoverned is called with equal-length arrays, the mapping governed for all modified addresses must be consistent with the updates made during that call, regardless of any subsequent assertGovernanceApproved call.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the total number of governed addresses remains unchanged.
After assertGovernanceApproved is called (whether it reverts or not), the governed mapping for any address viewed via public getter remains unchanged.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any valid addresses and emergency flag, the governed status of any address remains unchanged.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with a revert expected, the caller's governed status in the governed mapping remains the same as before the call.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with the same sender and target address, the second call in the same transaction always reverts.
If emergency is true, the transaction will always revert when block.timestamp - security.lastFlashGovernanceAct <= security.epochSize
When emergency is false, the transaction should succeed if the transfer succeeds and lock is expired, regardless of the epoch condition.
When emergency is true and the epoch condition fails, the reference contract reverts, but the buggy contract succeeds.
When emergency is false, the reference contract reverts if the epoch condition fails, but the buggy contract succeeds.

When emergency is true, the assertGovernanceApproved call reverts if the epoch condition fails; when emergency is false, it succeeds even if the epoch condition fails (provided transfer succeeds and lock is expired). This rule is broken by the mutant which inverts the emergency condition.
